**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The licence grant in § 13 meets our preferred position on every material term:

- **§ 13.1** — subscription grant runs to Customer, "its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," plus Authorized Users; worldwide, non-exclusive, and *not* labelled revocable or non-transferable.
- **§ 13.2** — paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables are licensed to Customer and its Affiliates on a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" basis, with modification/derivative rights and contractor support. **§ 14.3** confirms this licence reaches Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable.
- **§ 13.3** — transfer to an Affiliate or successor is permitted via § 24 (§ 24.1 allows M&A/asset-sale assignment without consent; § 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, suspending, or repricing on our change of control). Revocation or suspension is confined to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — no at-will revocation anywhere in the document (checked all "suspend" occurrences).
- **§ 13.4** — restrictions are ordinary and well-qualified ("knowingly," subject to Applicable Law, with carve-outs for authorized security testing and use of Customer Data and output); they do not narrow the grant.

This sits at the preferred position, not merely the fallback, so no changes are warranted.
